theorem: For identical register Hamiltonians, I-SWAP commutes with total energy. A constant pulse H_c=pi(I-SWAP)/(2 tau) implements SWAP exactly. Sudden on/off switching has zero net system-plus-interaction work because H_c is conserved during the pulse, although controller dissipation is outside the closed model. A finite-temperature Gibbs blank resets only to its excited probability delta=(1+e^{beta epsilon})^-1; an exact pure blank requires beta epsilon to diverge. Restoring the used ancilla to the Gibbs blank can extract at most its nonequilibrium free-energy excess, whereas preparing a low-error blank requires the displayed dimensionless gap.
